comparison_scope: Source-backed diagnostic comparison of llama.cpp Vulkan tg128 and retained hipEngine D9 c=1 decode on the same W7900 and exact UD-Q2_K_XL file; not a cross-engine product-throughput claim

matched_average_depth_tg31.purpose: Match hipEngine h32's 31 timed post-TTFT calls and its mean timed position 101.4 without claiming prompt or arithmetic equivalence

tg128_ablations.protocol: Same binary/model/device, -fa on, p0/n128, one warmup token, three repetitions; only the named environment variable changes

hipengine.sampling: GPU greedy argmax plus synchronized ID and max-logit scalar reads

differences: llama-bench clears state and times 128 forced-random one-token llama_decode calls at positions 0..127; hipEngine times natural greedy trajectories after 68..122-token prompts at positions 68..152.
llama-bench synchronizes each decode but does not sample, run device argmax, or read a token/logit; hipEngine includes its GPU argmax, device synchronization, and two scalar device-to-host reads.
llama.cpp uses F16 KV and a context sized to depth+generation; hipEngine uses BF16 KV with a 4096-token admitted allocation and KVLiveSpans.

llama-bench measures three long in-context repetitions after one warmup token; hipEngine aggregates two repetitions over ten category prompts and checks exact natural outputs, first-token KL/top-1, bulk state, and lifecycle.
Both exclude model load. llama-bench also excludes context construction and optional untimed depth setup; hipEngine decode excludes session construction and prefill.
protocol_comparison.conclusion: The published 93.67 tok/s is reproducible and protocol/context differences do not explain the approximately 2x model-step gap, but only a matched natural-token harness with the same sampling/readback and KV arithmetic can support a formal cross-engine throughput ratio.

source_findings.finding: llama-bench tg128 is forced-token model evaluation, not generated-token sampling
source_findings.evidence: Each iteration calls llama_decode on one random token, synchronizes, and assigns another random token; timing surrounds the complete test_gen call after memory clear.

source_findings.finding: Vulkan graph fusion is the largest directly measured control
source_findings.evidence: The backend detects and fuses multi-add, RMS/add, top-k MoE sigmoid/correction/normalization, matvec post-ops, and selected-down scaling; disabling fusion costs 2.777 ms/token and 20.79% throughput.

source_findings.finding: Graph reordering and dependency-scoped barriers are real but secondary in this tg128 control
source_findings.evidence: The backend synchronizes overlapping read/write dependencies and sorts the graph for parallelism; disabling graph optimization costs 0.116 ms/token and 1.08% throughput.

source_findings.finding: Q8_1 integer-dot MMVQ is not the Laguna c=1 optimum on this RADV/W7900 build
source_findings.evidence: The default AMD heuristic selects MMVQ for K>=2048 except Q8_0, but disabling MMVQ improves 0.435 ms/token and 4.29%; do not port Q8_1 quantization blindly.

source_findings.finding: The default trace places independent attention projections and routed/shared MoE branches in concurrent dependency groups
source_findings.evidence: Grouped records pair flash attention with query/gate projections, pair routed gate/up projections, and pair shared projections/adds; per-node timing mode intentionally serializes these groups and is not a wall-time decomposition.

source_findings.finding: The decode shaders use raw IQ2_XS/IQ3_XXS layouts and subgroup reductions
source_findings.evidence: Raw block layouts feed specialization-constant workgroups; result reduction uses subgroupAdd, with the W7900 reporting subgroup size 64.

transfer_priorities.candidate: Finish D11 exact persistent router/top-k contraction
transfer_priorities.rationale: It is already selected from a measured 0.896-ms adjacent D9 window, is one concrete slice of Vulkan's dominant fusion advantage, and has an exact in-tree persistent-counter precedent.
transfer_priorities.expected_bound: 47 fewer dispatches/token; full-window zero-cost ceiling 49.21 tok/s, so not target closure alone

transfer_priorities.candidate: Audit and port exact Vulkan-style raw Q5 attention-output and query/gate GEMV geometry
transfer_priorities.rationale: These are D9's 2.659- and 2.189-ms short families and Vulkan's trace shows materially shorter fused/grouped Q5 windows. This is distinct from the rejected HIP tile16 traffic-sharing design.
transfer_priorities.gate: Preserve hipEngine's current BF16/reduction contract, compare actual K6144/K9216/K3072 weights, require scratch0 and both production shapes faster before model runs

transfer_priorities.candidate: Extend exact graph-level post-op fusion around Q5 output, IQ3 selected-down weighting, and shared/routed combines
transfer_priorities.rationale: Disabling all Vulkan fusions costs 2.777 ms/token; hipEngine D9 has removed only bounded pair/tail launches and still dispatches 775 kernels/token.
transfer_priorities.gate: One fusion boundary at a time with registered primitive fallback and full category non-regression; do not infer the whole Vulkan ablation transfers additively

transfer_priorities.candidate: Prototype a source-backed one-wave raw attention kernel rather than token16 extrapolation
transfer_priorities.rationale: D9 short SWA+global attention is about 2.67 ms/token and Vulkan flash-attention groups are much shorter, but D10 token8 failed the full category policy despite mechanical wins.
transfer_priorities.gate: New algorithm/geometry, complete KVLiveSpans and exact-order proof; no promotion from a single context or token8 barrier arithmetic

transfer_priorities.candidate: Defer generic graph replay, stream overlap, and Q8_1 MMVQ
transfer_priorities.rationale: hipEngine graph replay and prior stream tactics regressed; Vulkan graph ordering is only a 0.116-ms control; disabling Vulkan MMVQ is faster by 4.29%.
transfer_priorities.gate: Reopen only with a new measured mechanism, not source analogy

notes: The Vulkan perf logger perturbs and can serialize dependency groups; its operator totals are attribution evidence, not the 94.5 tok/s wall.
The user-reported 93.67 +/- 0.16 tok/s is independently reproduced at 94.513 +/- 0.141 tok/s on the same file/device.
The matched-depth control remains around 94.15 tok/s, so starting-context depth is not the source of the gap.
